Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's all we have from this game. The match has been abandoned due to rain, and Bangladesh have clinched the series 2-0. The Netherlands side will take a break from cricket, while Bangladesh advances to the Asia Cup, where they open against Hong Kong on 11 September at 2.30 pm GMT. Do join us for the early build-up as well. Until then, take care, and cheers!

Litton Das proudly accepts the trophy after the post-match interview, passing it on to his teammates. They gather in front of the 'winners' board, beaming with joy as they snap pictures with the trophy in hand. The elation on the faces of the Bangladesh players and coaching staff is unmistakable, embodying the triumph of their relentless effort and unwavering spirit. This is not just a celebration, it’s a powerful testament to their hard work and commitment that led them to this incredible victory!

The skipper of Litton Das wins the Player of the Series for his outstanding performance with his bat. He says that the batters in the last two games didn't really get the time to showcase their batting prowess in the middle, but today, he is happy to see that they are ready for the upcoming challenges. He gives the credit to the opposition team for putting all the efforts coming in their country in short notice. Ends up saying that he has faith that the Netherlands will do good in their future.

The skipper of Netherlands, Scott Edwards says that they would love to have some batting but the rains spoiled the plans. Also give credit to the opposition batters, the way they batted, but he is also grateful that his bowlers fought back and tried to gain control of the match. Ends up saying that after going back to the their country the players will have some rest and then go to different parts of the world to continue their careers.
The Presentation ceremony...

After the rain interruption, the Netherlands bowlers did a great job in keeping the Bangladesh batters under wraps. Kyle Klein stepped up in the 14th over, picking up the crucial wickets of Litton Das and Shamim Hossain. Das's departure for a magnificent 73 runs was the highlight of the game. Tim Pringle was the pick of the bowlers for the Netherlands as he was economical and picked up a wicket. Nurul Hasan and Jaker Ali unleashed their batting brilliance, putting on a stunning display that had everyone on the edge of their seats. Unfortunately, just as they were gaining momentum, the rain gods intervened, forcing the match officials to call for an innings break, and that was it.

So, to summarise, Bangladesh's innings came to a close at 164 runs, and what a start they had! Litton Das was in imperious form, smashing boundaries and keeping the scoreboard ticking. They were off to a flying start, but Litton Das was dropped twice by Shariz Ahmad before the rain break, and he made the most of his chances. They were 60/1 at 4.1 overs when the rain came in.

UPDATE - 3.49 pm GMT - THE MATCH HAS BEEN ABANDONED DUE TO RAIN! The rain gods showed no mercy, and after multiple stoppages of the live contest, the match officials have decided to call off the match.

UPDATE - 3.38 pm GMT - Bad news folks! The showers of rain have started, and more covers are coming in from the side of the field of play! The cut-off time for the Dutch side’s 5-over run chase is set at 3:48 pm GMT. Stay tuned for more updates!

While we wait for the rain to cease, here's what happened at the Harare Sports Club. Sri Lanka edged out Zimbabwe in a thrilling T20I opener, chasing down 176 runs with 4 wickets to spare. The hosts posted 175, thanks to Brian Bennett's impressive 81. Dushmantha Chameera starred with the ball for Sri Lanka, claiming 3 wickets. In response, Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis blasted off to a 96-run opening partnership before Tinotenda Maposa broke the stand. Despite losing key wickets, Kamindu Mendis stepped up, smashing 41. He and debutant, Dushan Hemantha shared an unbeaten 35-run stand towards the end to guide Sri Lanka to victory.
UPDATE - 2.51 pm GMT - It looks like the rain has stopped now, and we can see some of the groundsmen waiting for some instructions to remove the covers from the pitch. Stay tuned for more updates...

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Litton Das and Saif Hassan walk in with their blades for Bangladesh. Aryan Dutt has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Pitch Report - Farveez Maharoof is pitchside. He says that there are a few cracks on the ground, but it won't affect the flurry of runs much. He adds that the bowlers will have to bowl on good lengths and restrict the batters.

Litton Das, the skipper of Bangladesh, says that they are okay to bat first. Adds that they will try to post a good score. He says that they will look to put a total over 180. Ends by saying that they have five changes as some of their big players need to get rest for the big event.

Scott Edwards, the skipper of Netherlands, says that they will bowl first. Adds that there will be dew later in the game, and there is an opportunity for them to prove something. He says that they need some early wickets and they need to restrict them to a par score. Ends by saying that Tim Pringle is back in the side.

Netherlands (Playing XI) - Max O'Dowd, Vikramjit Singh, Teja Nidamanuru, Scott Edwards (C)(WK), Shariz Ahmad, Noah Croes, Tim Pringle (In for Sikander Zulfiqar), Kyle Klein, Aryan Dutt, Paul van Meekeren, Daniel Doram.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Litton Das (C)(WK), Saif Hassan, Tawhid Hridoy, Nurul Hasan (In for Tanzid Hasan), Jaker Ali, Shamim Hossain (In for Parvez Hossain Emon), Mohammad Saifuddin (In for Tanzim Hasan Sakib), Shoriful Islam (In for Mustafizur Rahman), Rishad Hossain (In for Mahedi Hasan), Nasum Ahmed, Tanzim Hasan Sakib.
TOSS - Netherlands have won the toss and will BOWL first.
As the match unfolds, both sides will be eager to showcase form and flair ahead of bigger assignment. Can Bangladesh complete a clean sweep? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit...

Bangladesh’s lineup looks forged for momentum. Parvez Hossain Emon and Tanzid Hasan Tamim have laid a solid foundation, with Litton Das ready to back them up while remaining unbeaten. The surface at Sylhet favors quick scoring and smart seam bowling, so expect the hosts to apply early pressure and build through the powerplay, while Nasum Ahmed and the seam attack look to trap the Dutch early.

The Dutch will hope for a steadier effort with the bat this time, aiming to post a more competitive total and test Bangladesh’s shaky, yet improving, middle-overs approach. After a disciplined bowling performance in the previous game, the visitors will need their top order to fire and their lower middle order to contribute valuable runs to convert pressure into points on the scoreboard.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! Bangladesh return to Sylhet for the final flourish of a three-match T20I series, looking to seal a clean sweep against the Netherlands and cap off a productive warm-up ahead of the Asia Cup. The home side have already impressed with their aggressive openers and tight bowling, setting a strong tone for what promises to be an entertaining game.

Bangladesh are eyeing a clean sweep as they take on the Netherlands in the third and final T20I in Sylhet, having dominated the series so far with wins by eight and nine wickets. The hosts have been clinical in all departments, with Tanzid Hasan’s blistering knocks at the top setting the tone, and Litton Das and Tawhid Hridoy adding solidity in the middle order. Taskin Ahmed’s fiery pace and Nasum Ahmed’s crafty spin have kept the Dutch batters in check, with Rishad Hossain’s variations also proving effective. Their strength lies in the bowling depth and power-packed batting lineup, while a minor concern has been occasional lapses in fielding. Netherlands, on the other hand, have struggled for consistency, relying heavily on Vikramjit Singh and Max O'Dowd for runs, while Aryan Dutt and Kyle Klein have done well, but the likes of Paul van Meekeren and Tim Pringle needs to do a lot better with the ball. Their key weakness has been failing to build partnerships and handle Bangladesh’s spin threat. With the series already decided, the hosts may rotate their squad to test bench strength, while the Dutch will aim to find balance and salvage pride.
